Can you name all 4 superficial forearm flexors? One hand does it ✋
Superficial forearm flexors mnemonic: Pass, Fail, Pass, Fail
P = Pronator teres (index finger)
F = Flexor carpi radialis (middle finger)
P = Palmaris longus (ring finger)
F = Flexor carpi ulnaris (little finger)
(thumb side → pinky side)
Hand trick: put the heel of your other hand on the bony bump inside your elbow (the medial epicondyle) and spread your fingers down your forearm. All four share that starting point.
Quick test: which one is supplied by the ulnar nerve? Answer in the video.
Save this for your next anatomy exam.
Images: Gray's Anatomy (1918), Fig. 414, public domain; diagrams: Book Plume

pin_desc: Superficial forearm flexors mnemonic for anatomy class: Pass, Fail, Pass, Fail = pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus and flexor carpi ulnaris, thumb side to pinky side. Hand trick: heel of your other hand on the medial epicondyle, fingers spread down the forearm. Only flexor carpi ulnaris gets the ulnar nerve; the other three get the median nerve.
